answer: A dune restoration market hires agents to manage nearby lotus pools. Each bid spends a nontransferable work credit earned when an unrelated buyer confirms a finished job and a random auditor checks it. A public mirror of the payment graph flags circular trades, so fifty aliases cannot recycle one job into fifty credits. To place fifty bids, an attacker must finish fifty checked jobs or bribe buyers and auditors, spending labor, fees and time. Small honest teams may look clustered, and bribery can pass the graph check, so flagged credits get an appeal and surprise audits.
